name: Android ID (SSAID)
plain: A 64-bit ID per app signing key and user on Android; changes on factory reset.
meaning: Gives a stable per-developer device ID with no prompt. Since Android 8 apps signed by different developers see different values.

android.persistence: Until factory reset or signing key change
android.store_policy: Play: use the advertising ID for ads, not this
android.note: 64-bit value as 16 hex characters; scoped to signing key, user and device since Android 8

limits.headline: Can recognize your Android phone with a long ID, separate for each app maker
limits.user_action: Nothing. Any Android app can ask for it with no prompt
can: Use a 16 character ID to tell your phone and user profile apart
Keep recognizing you across restarts and app updates
Link your activity across apps signed by the same developer
cannot: Match you across apps from different developers on Android 8 and newer
Survive a factory reset; a new ID is made
Exist on iPhone; the closest match is the vendor ID, which works differently
limits.differs: Android only. iPhone has no Android ID; its closest match is the vendor ID.

story.what_it_is: A long ID Android keeps for each developer's apps on one phone.

marketing.name: Android ID (SSAID)
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: a 64 bit value that is unique per app signing key and user, and resets on factory reset.

story.for_you: You never see it and it asks nothing. It lets one company recognize your phone across its apps, and it changes only if you factory reset or the developer changes signing keys.
story.for_makers: Gives developers a stable ID without any permission. It is used for saved accounts, fraud checks and tying installs together, though Google tells developers to prefer other IDs for ads.

use_cases.example: A game restores your progress on a re-installed copy of the game because it sees the same ID as before.
A payments app counts how many accounts used one phone ID and blocks the tenth.
An ad attribution tool uses it to tie an install to a click when the ad ID has been turned off.
A coupon app makes sure a one time welcome offer is not redeemed again on the same phone.
A product team counts unique devices over months without asking for a login.
A company device manager uses it to know which phone is which in its fleet.

risks: Easy to join with other data
story.android_note: Per app signing key and user since Android 8, so different developers see different values.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no SSAID; the closest is the vendor ID.
